title: The Mad plan for the roof
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：mad　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mad 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the musician wrote of ① a mad plan for the roof in the programme, and everybody in the hall said at once that it was ② madder than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the musician, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the mad ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the maddest plan for the roof anybody in the hall had ever seen, or so the programme for December 1974 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too mad to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the mad ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a mad look from the teacher, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as mad as the look from the teacher they had once had in the old hall. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was mad or not, and he said so.

By 1987 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something mad, and nothing besides. The listener from the next hall called the whole plan ⑧ quite mad; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the mad ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1990, twice over, she wrote of another mad plan for the roof in the same programme, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ madder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The maddest look from the teacher in the whole hall, she said in 1992, was the one she could never quite name; the mad ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 疯狂（前置定语 a mad plan for the roof：1980 年乐师在节目单里记下的那件疯狂的方案）
B. adj. 疯狂／恼火（比较级 madder than：文中两处，一处比屋顶那个疯狂的方案，一处比预想）
C. adj. 疯狂／恼火（最高级 the maddest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 疯狂（表语 too mad to do：母亲觉得它太疯狂，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 恼火（前置定语 a mad look from the teacher：叔叔把整件事称作一桩恼火的眼神）
F. adj. 恼火（同级比较 as mad as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩老师恼火的眼神相比）
G. adj. 恼火（后置定语 something mad：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 恼火（受程度副词修饰 quite mad：那位听客的评价）

items.q: a mad plan for the roof
the maddest plan for the roof anybody
a mad look from the teacher
The maddest look from the teacher in

answers.why: mad 意为“疯狂”，1980 年乐师在节目单里记下的是“一件疯狂的方案”，此处作前置定语 a mad plan for the roof。
mad 意为“疯狂”，此处用比较级 madder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
mad 意为“疯狂”，节目单上 十二月 那行字说它是音乐厅里最疯狂的一件，故用最高级 the maddest plan for the roof。
mad 意为“疯狂”，母亲认为这件东西“太疯狂了，谁也用不上”，too mad to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
mad 意为“恼火”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩恼火的眼神”，此处作前置定语 a mad look from the teacher。
mad 意为“恼火”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩老师恼火的眼神一样恼火”，同级比较用 as mad as。
mad 意为“恼火”，节目单上那半行字要的是“恼火的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something mad。
mad 意为“恼火”，邻音乐厅来的那位听客认为这套计划“相当恼火”，quite 修饰原级 mad。
mad 意为“恼火”，1990 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要恼火”，故用比较级 madder than。
mad 意为“恼火”，母亲 1992 年说的是“整个音乐厅里最恼火的那一桩”，故用最高级 the maddest look from the teacher。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1980 年，乐师在节目单里记下了一件疯狂的方案。（a mad plan for the roof）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更疯狂。（madder than …）
母亲觉得它太疯狂，谁也用不上。（too mad to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩恼火的眼神。（a mad look from the teacher）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩老师恼火的眼神一样恼火。（as mad as …）
到了 1987 年，节目单上只剩半行字：要的是一件恼火的东西。（something mad）
answers: In 1980 the musician wrote of a mad plan for the roof in the programme.
Everybody said it was madder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too mad to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a mad look from the teacher.
He said nobody would call it as mad as the look from the teacher they had once had.
By 1987 the programme asked for nothing but something mad.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 mad 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the musician wrote of a mad plan for the roof in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the maddest plan for the roof in the hall, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too mad to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a mad look from the teacher, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next hall called the plan quite mad, and everybody laughed.
The mad ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
